I answered B from domain reasoning, not from a statistical test. The data doesn't separate A from B.

In `arctic.csv`, Residual_heat_flux and Residual_SLP are almost uncorrelated (r ≈ 0.06 across 468 rows). So the data alone gives little sign of a strong link in either direction. A correlation of this kind can't show which way causation runs.

Physically, sea level pressure sets the large-scale atmospheric circulation. That circulation drives winds and heat transport, which in turn change the surface heat flux. The reverse is much less plausible, since local surface heat flux is unlikely to shift the large-scale pressure field. I therefore chose "SLP causes heat flux" over the other options. Option D is possible given the weak correlation, but it is less likely than a real SLP-to-heat-flux effect.

ANSWER: B
